item.title: Vixens stun GIANTS
item.description: By Alexander DabbThe Melbourne Vixens made an emphatic statement at Qudos Bank Arena on Sunday afternoon, notching a second win from as many games to open their premiership defence with a dominant 68-52 victory over the GIANTS.With the two sides at different ends of the experience spectrum, it was the Vixens that proved a class above, widening the gap at every break to claim a second straight double-digit win.

item.title: A proud finish
item.description: By Pip Turton The Sydney double header delivered a thriller at Qudos Bank Arena, where the NSW Swifts edged out the Melbourne Mavericks 70 to 69 in a high-intensity contest that had a record Sydney crowd of over 13,000 on the edge of their seats. The Swifts entered the match hungry for redemption, chasing their first win since the start of last season in front of a home crowd, the Mavericks on the other hand arrived determined to make a statement.

item.title: National junior netball guidelines updated
item.description: Netball Australia has released new National Junior Netball Guidelines, which focus on providing a safe, fun and inclusive environment for all people. The guidelines provide a framework for Member Organisations, affiliated associations and clubs, schools, community sport service organisations and other groups responsible for the development, organisation and delivery of junior netballers aged five to 18 years.

item.title: Melbourne Derby goes to extra time
item.description: By Pip Turton What a performance at John Cain Arena, and what a way to showcase a Melbourne derby. Sixty minutes was not enough to separate these two sides, with the Vixens and Mavericks delivering a match packed with intensity, momentum swings and pure netball drama before it was finally decided in extra time.

item.title: Is another thriller lined up?
item.description: By Stephanie SmarrelliLast weekend the Swifts and Lightning walked away with four points by the skin of their teeth.With momentum on the line, Round 3 is shaping up for them to make an early-season statement. The Swifts are aiming to break into the top four while Lightning are fighting to stay there and neither side can afford to blink.They both survived last week but they’ll want to really own this one as the competition heats up.

item.title: Why Wilson backs the bid
item.description: By Vicki WilsonWalking to school with a friend during the 1976 Montreal Olympics, we pretended we were Nadia Comaneci doing her famous routine on the balance beam. I didn’t want to be a gymnast; as a junior netballer, a very tall one, I was never going to be.But most people have a first Olympic moment, and that was mine. For a while there, every neighbourhood fence was my stage. Not falling off was almost as good as a medal.

item.title: Why you can’t miss the Melb derby
item.description: This weekend, John Cain Arena will finally come alive.And the city will be divided.The Melbourne derby is here and with the Melbourne Mavericks desperate to show up their city rivals, you surely cannot miss this one.Yes, there will be netball. With the epic showdown between the Mavs and Vixens taking place on the court. item.title: Lightning edge Swifts in thriller
item.description: The NSW Swifts wasted no time asserting themselves, opening the scoring inside the first minute before capitalising on a Sunshine Coast error to surge to an early 3-0 lead, courtesy of a brilliant play from Teigan O’Shannassy.

item.title: Fever thrash GIANTS
item.description: By Madeline IrwinThe West Coast Fever kept the GIANTS winless start to the season going with a thumping 19-goal win in front of their home crowd at RAC Arena on Sunday.

item.title: Thunderbirds storm to biggest ever win
item.description: By Alexander DabbIf double digit wins in the first two rounds weren't scary enough, the Adelaide Thunderbirds’ Round 3 performance against the Queensland Firebirds should be.In a dominant showing from first whistle to final buzzer, all 10 players took to the court as the Thunderbirds made it three wins on the trot with their biggest ever margin of victory in Suncorp Super Netball, prevailing by 27 goals in a devastating 73 to 46 victory at Nissan Arena in Brisbane on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Talking points: Round 3
item.description: By Sophie TaylorSaturday matches reigned supreme throughout a blockbuster round of activity boasting down-to-the-wire finishes and two big results.We run through some of the major talking points from the weekend. LADDER HEATING UPThe undeniable Thunderbirds hold top spot on the ladder and, ominously, make no signs of shifting from that spot.With their extra time win on the board this week the Vixens retain second spot with a flawless record on paper.

item.title: Apply now: CGF Natural Disaster Relief Fund
item.description: In partnership with Suncorp, the Confident Girls Foundation is supporting netball communities affected by natural disaster through the Natural Disaster Relief Fund.The deadline for this year’s fund is fast approaching with applications closing Tuesday 14 April.Eligible netball clubs, associations and community groups can apply for grants of up to $5,000 to aid their recovery efforts to rebuild in the wake of devastating bushfires, floods and other weather events.

item.title: Easter Sunday showdown
item.description: By Stephanie SmarrelliJust weeks into the 2026 season and the gap between the contenders and chasers is already opening, with tight finishes, one-goal thrillers and statement wins setting the tone early.This weekend the pressure is only going to intensify. Two genuine contenders go head-to-head but they’ve had two very different starts to the season.West Coast Fever have been fairly in control, two wins from three games they’re in the top half of the ladder, exactly where they want to be.
